prompt: Complete DateFormatterUtil: pretty formats a LocalDate as "MMM dd, yyyy" in Locale.US (e.g. "Mar 05, 2026"), and parseSlash parses strings like "3/5/2026" with the pattern "M/d/yyyy".
explanation: In the pattern, MMM is the short month NAME, which depends on the locale -- passing Locale.US to ofPattern pins it to English abbreviations like "Mar" no matter what machine runs the code, while dd zero-pads the day. For parsing, single-letter M and d accept one or two digits, so the same formatter reads both "3/5/2026" and "12/31/1999"; LocalDate.parse(text, formatter) applies it. DateTimeFormatter objects are immutable and thread-safe, so building them once as constants is idiomatic.
hints: Build the formatter once with DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern, passing Locale.US as a second argument, then let the date format itself with it.
Without the Locale argument, MMM would use the computer's default language -- the tests demand English month names.
For parsing, create a formatter from "M/d/yyyy" and call LocalDate.parse(s, formatter); one-letter M and d happily accept one- or two-digit numbers.
